mainTopic: Aggadic teachings built on פסוקים: hard learning and its fixes, prayer and rain, pride and quarrels, לשון הרע, sincere prayer (יחיד vs. ציבור), faithful people, and closed heavens.
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing ריש לקיש's teaching: learning feels hard as iron when a student's משנה is not organized, so he should review more, as ריש לקיש and רב אדא בר אהבה did. רבא reads the same פסוק differently: the problem is a רבי who is not warm to the student, and the fix is to send friends to make peace. רבי אמי then teaches that rain is held back when no one knows how to pray properly. He gives a ladder of fixes: go to someone who can pray, and if that fails, go to the חסיד of the generation. A person who becomes proud after his prayer is answered brings anger to the world, and so do two scholars who are harsh with each other. ריש לקיש reads the snake verse as a lesson about לשון הרע. The גמרא resolves a challenge to רבי אמi's rule about sincere prayer: an individual needs a sincere heart, but a ציבור is answered even without it. Teachings follow about faithful people bringing rain, exacting judgment for those who are exacting with themselves, and joy in suffering. The עמוד ends with ריש לקיש comparing closed heavens to a woman in labor who cannot give birth, a comparison that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Hard learning comes from an unorganized משנה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's statement (begun on 7b) finishes: a תלמיד whose learning is hard as iron has this problem because his משנה is not organized for him. The proof is the פסוק ‘וְהוּא לֹא פָנִים קִלְקַל’.
steps.simpleTranslation: …whose learning is as hard for him as iron, this is because his משנה is not organized for him, as it says: “And he did not sharpen the face.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing ריש לקיש's statement from the end of 7b. He explains why some students find learning so hard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads ‘פָנִים’ as the ‘surface’ of learning, meaning the basic משנה. ‘קִלְקַל’ can also mean ‘spoiled.’ If the base text is messy, everything built on it, like the גמרא, becomes as hard as iron.

keyTerms.meaning: his learning (the analysis and גמרא he studies)
his משנה (the basic text he learned)
face or surface; here, the basic ‘surface’ layer of learning

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The speaker is ריש לקיש, who began ‘אם ראית תלמיד…’ on the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: whose learning is as hard for him as iron —
phrases.notes: Continues ‘If you see a student…’ from 7b.

phrases.english: it is because his Mishnah is not organized for him,
as it says: “And he did not sharpen (or: spoiled) the face (surface).”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's statement begun on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning is hard as iron when the student's basic משנה is not clearly organized in his mind.

steps.title: What is the remedy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what such a student should do to fix his problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short practical question. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the cause is known (an unorganized משנה), the natural next question is how to repair it. The question is not an attack. It looks for a practical solution.

phrases.english: What is his remedy? —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a solution to the problem described in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a student whose משנה is disorganized fix his difficulty?

steps.title: Sit and learn more, and better yet, organize from the start
steps.stepSummary: The fix is to spend more time sitting and learning, from ‘וַחֲיָלִים יְגַבֵּר’. The end of the פסוק, ‘וְיִתְרוֹן הַכְשֵׁיר חׇכְמָה’, teaches that it is even better if the משנה was organized from the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should increase his sitting and learning, as it says: “He must add strength, and wisdom is an advantage that makes things right.” All the more so if his משנה is organized for him from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The struggling student must put in extra hours. The best plan is to organize the משנה well from the beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ‘Add strength’ means extra effort, which here means more time in ישיבה. ‘Wisdom is an advantage’ adds a second point: preventing the problem is better than fixing it later.

keyTerms.meaning: he should increase his sitting (in study)

phrases.english: he should increase his sitting (in study),
as it says: “Then he must add strength,”
“and wisdom is an advantage that sets things right.”
All the more so if his Mishnah
is organized for him from the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Study more hours. Best of all, organize the משנה properly from the start.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic Talmudic source for heavy חזרה (review) and clear basics before deeper analysis.

steps.title: ריש לקיש and רב אדא בר אהבה reviewed many times before going to their teachers
steps.stepSummary: Two examples of organizing the משנה ‘from the beginning’. ריש לקיש reviewed 40 times, matching the 40 days the תורה was given, before going to רבי יוחנן. רב אדא בר אהבה reviewed 24 times, matching the 24 books of תנ״ך, before going to רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like ריש לקיש, who would review his משנה forty times, matching the forty days in which the תורה was given, and then go in to רבי יוחנן. רב אדא בר אהבה would review his משנה twenty-four times, matching תורה, נביאים and כתובים, and then go in to רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two real-life examples of great חכמים who organized their learning thoroughly before going to their רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These stories illustrate the ‘כל שכן’ idea: master the basics first. Each number is tied to a symbol of תורה, 40 days at סיני or 24 books of תנ״ך. That shows review was treated as a form of receiving the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: and would go in before (his teacher)

steps.whatToRemember: Main lesson of ריש לקיש's line: a clear, well-reviewed משנה is the key to understanding. Great חכמים reviewed dozens of times before learning with their רבי.

phrases.english: Like this practice of Reish Lakish:
he would review his Mishnah forty times,
corresponding to the forty days in which the Torah was given,
and then go in before Rabbi Yochanan.
Rav Adda bar Ahava
would review his Mishnah twenty-four times,
corresponding to Torah, Prophets, and Writings,
and then go in before Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the ‘organized from the beginning’ ideal of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The value of organizing one's משנה before deeper study.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practices of ריש לקיש (40 reviews) and רב אדא בר אהבה (24 reviews).

steps.title: רבא: the problem is a teacher who is not friendly
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the same פסוק differently. Learning is hard as iron because the student's רבי does not show him a friendly face. Here ‘פָנִים’ means ‘face/countenance’.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If you see a student whose learning is as hard for him as iron, it is because his רבי does not show him a friendly face, as it says: “And he did not sharpen the face.”
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different explanation of the same פסוק. He blames the teacher's attitude instead of the student's disorganized learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש read ‘פָנִים’ as the ‘surface’ (the basic משנה). רבא reads it as a literal ‘face’, meaning the teacher's expression. A stern, harsh רבי blocks the student's understanding, so the fix lies with the teacher's warmth.

keyTerms.meaning: shows him a friendly face / pleasant manner

steps.whyThisMatters: It adds a responsibility on the רבי. A student's struggle may come from the teacher's harshness, not only the student's weakness.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If you see a student
whose learning is as hard for him as iron —

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁבִיל רַבּוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַסְבִּיר לוֹ פָּנִים,
phrases.english: it is because his teacher does not show him a friendly face,
as it says: “And he did not sharpen the face.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק used by ריש לקיש in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student's hard learning can come from a רבי who does not show him a pleasant, encouraging face.

steps.title: What should this student do?
steps.stepSummary: Following רבא's reading, the גמרא asks how a student whose רבי is not friendly to him can fix the problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step. If the problem is that the רבי is cold to the student, what can the student do about it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds exactly like the question in Step 2, but it belongs to a different reading. In Step 2 the problem was messy learning. Here, following רבא, the problem is a strained relationship with the רבי, so it needs a different fix.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the question in Step 2. The words are the same, but this question is asked according to רבא's reading, where the problem is the רבי's unfriendly face, not disorganized learning.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?
phrases.notes: The question is asked according to רבא's reading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical fix to the problem רבא just described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a student with a cold רבי can repair the situation.

steps.title: Send many friends to make peace with the רבי
steps.stepSummary: The student should get many friends to speak to the רבי for him, read from 'וַחֲיָלִים יְגַבֵּר'. It is even better if he acted properly before his רבי from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should bring many friends to speak for him, as it says: 'He must increase חֲיָלִים (strength/companions); and wisdom is the advantage of setting things right.' All the more so it is better if his deeds were proper before his רבי from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבא's fix. The student should gather many friends who will go to the רבי and make peace for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חֲיָלִים' is read as 'companions' instead of 'strength.' The end of the פסוק is read the same way as before: prevention beats repair. This time it means that if he had behaved properly toward his רבי from the start, he would never have needed these friends.
steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of the פסוק follow the same pattern: there is a fix after the problem starts, but it is much better to prevent the problem from the beginning.

phrases.english: he should increase friends on his behalf,
phrases.notes: Friends who will speak to the רבי for him.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'Then he must increase strength (troops)'
'but wisdom is the advantage of setting right.'
All the more so if his deeds were made proper
before his teacher from the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6 and finishes רבא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gather many friends to make peace with the רבי. Proper behavior from the start is even better.

steps.title: Rain is held back when no one knows how to pray
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains 'אִם יִשֹּׁךְ הַנָּחָשׁ בְּלוֹא לָחַשׁ'. When the heavens 'rust' like copper and give no rain, it is because the generation has no one who 'whispers' prayers properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: What does the פסוק mean, 'If the snake bites without a whisper (charm), the master of the tongue has no advantage'? If you see a generation whose heavens rust like copper and do not bring down dew and rain, it is because there are no people in that generation who whisper prayers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main topic, rain, with a new teaching from רבי אמי. He reads a פסוק about snakes as a lesson about prayer and rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is wordplay. 'יִשֹּׁךְ' is read like 'מִשְׁתַּכִּין' (rusting), 'נָּחָשׁ' like 'נְחֹשֶׁת' (copper), and 'לָחַשׁ' as quiet prayer. The meaning: when the sky is shut 'like rusted copper,' the cause is that no one in the generation knows how to pray properly.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written
whispering; here, those who pray quiet, proper prayers

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'If the snake bites without a charm (whisper),'
'then the master of the tongue has no advantage'?
If you see a generation
whose heavens rust like copper
so they do not bring down dew and rain,
it is because there are no whisperers of whispers (people who pray) in the generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching. It returns from the topic of students to the larger topic of rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lack of rain comes from the absence of people in the generation who know how to pray properly.

steps.title: What should such a generation do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the fix is for a generation that has no proper prayers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is their fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: what can the people do if the rain is held back?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier part of the דף. First the problem is named, then the fix is asked for. Here the 'patient' is the whole generation, so the question is in the plural (תַּקָּנָתָן).

phrases.english: What is their remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the fix to the problem רבי אמי described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a rainless generation should do.

steps.title: Go to someone who knows how to pray
steps.stepSummary: They should go to someone who knows how to 'whisper' (pray properly). The source is 'יַגִּיד עָלָיו רֵעוֹ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They should go to someone who knows how to whisper (pray), as it is written: 'His friend will speak for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the people should turn to a person who knows how to pray, so he can pray for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק from איוב is read as: a 'friend' who knows how to pray will 'speak up' to ה׳ on the people's behalf. So the missing skill can be borrowed from someone who has it.

keyTerms.meaning: his friend will speak for him (איוב לו:לג)

phrases.english: They should go to one who knows how to whisper (pray),
as it is written: 'His friend will speak concerning him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Go to someone who knows how to pray and have him pray for them.

steps.title: Someone who can pray but does not gains nothing
steps.stepSummary: The end of the פסוק, 'וְאֵין יִתְרוֹן לְבַעַל הַלָּשׁוֹן', is explained: a person who is able to pray but does not gets no benefit from his ability.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the master of the tongue has no advantage': a person who is able to whisper (pray) but does not, what benefit does he have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the last part of the פסוק from קהלת. It is a criticism of a person who has the ability to pray and does not use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בַעַל הַלָּשׁוֹן' is the person who has the skill to pray. His skill is worth nothing if he stays silent while the generation suffers. So the פסוק blames not only the lack of praying people, but also people who could pray and do not.

keyTerms.meaning: master of the tongue: someone with the ability to pray

phrases.english: 'And the master of the tongue has no advantage':

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִלְחוֹשׁ וְאֵינוֹ לוֹחֵשׁ,
phrases.english: and one who is able to whisper (pray) but does not whisper,
what benefit is there to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes reading the קהלת פסוק that רבי אמי began explaining in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ability to pray that is not used has no value.

steps.title: What if he prayed and was not answered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what to do if someone prayed and still got no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he whispered (prayed) and was not answered, what is his fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question to set up the next step. What happens when even the prayer did not work?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes the discussion one level deeper. The earlier fix was to find someone who knows how to pray. Now the גמרא asks what to do when that kind of prayer has already been tried and failed.

phrases.english: And if he whispered (prayed) and was not answered,
what is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 10 by asking about the case where the prayer failed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The next step when prayer is not answered.

steps.title: Go to the חסיד of the generation, who will pray hard
steps.stepSummary: He should go to the חסיד of the generation, who will pray a great deal for him. The source is 'וַיְצַו עָלֶיהָ בְּמַפְגִּיעַ'. 'פגיעה' means prayer, as shown from ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should go to the pious man of the generation, who will pray a lot for him, as it says: 'He commanded it because of one who implores (מַפְגִּיעַ).' And 'פגיעה' always means prayer, as it says: 'And you, do not pray for this nation, do not raise for them cry or prayer, and do not implore (תִּפְגַּע) Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final fix: go to the most pious person of the generation and have him pray intensely. It then proves from a second פסוק that the word 'מַפְגִּיעַ' refers to prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב (one פסוק before 'יַגִּיד עָלָיו רֵעוֹ') says ה׳ gives the rain command 'בְּמַפְגִּיעַ,' because of someone who implores. To show that 'פגיעה' means prayer, the גמרא quotes ירמיהו, where 'אַל תִּפְגַּע בִּי' appears right next to 'אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל.' That shows the two words have the same meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: the pious person of the generation
imploring; the גמרא says it means prayer

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's ladder for a drought: (1) the cause is a lack of people who pray properly; (2) go to someone who knows how to pray; (3) if that fails, go to the חסיד of the generation, who will pray a lot. 'פגיעה' = prayer.

phrases.english: He should go to the pious one of the generation,
and he (the pious one) will increase prayer on his behalf,
as it is said: 'And He commanded it because of one who implores.'
And 'imploring' is nothing other than prayer,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל בְּעַד הָעָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: as it is said: 'And you, do not pray for this nation,'
'and do not raise for them a cry or prayer,'
'and do not implore Me.'
phrases.notes: פגיעה appears alongside תפילה, so it means prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 and supports the answer with a word-meaning proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Go to the חסיד of the generation, who will pray intensely for him. 'מַפְגִּיעַ' means one who prays, proven from ירמיהו.
steps.raayaObject: That 'פגיעה' in איוב לו:לב means prayer.

steps.title: Pride after a successful prayer brings anger
steps.stepSummary: If someone prays properly and his prayer is answered, but he becomes proud because of it, he brings anger into the world. The source is 'מקנה אף על עולה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he whispered his prayer and it succeeded, but he becomes proud of himself, he brings anger into the world. As the verse says: 'Anger is acquired by one who raises himself up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the chain about prayer. It now warns the person whose prayer was answered not to become arrogant about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps praised a person who knows how to pray (לחש). Now the גמרא adds a danger: success can lead to pride. The verse 'מקנה אף על עולה' is read as a דרשה: אף (anger) is acquired (מקנה) because of one who 'goes up' (עולה), meaning one who raises himself in pride.

keyTerms.meaning: Whispered, meaning he prayed properly and with focus
It succeeded for him, meaning his prayer was answered
Read here as: anger is acquired by one who raises himself up

steps.confusionAlert: In its plain meaning, the verse in איוב talks about cattle (מקנה) and a rising storm. The גמרא is not translating it literally. It reads the words in a new way to teach a lesson about pride.

phrases.english: And if he whispered (prayed) and it succeeded for him,
and he becomes proud of himself —
he brings anger to the world,
as it says: 'Anger is acquired by one who raises himself up.'
phrases.notes: Literally in איוב: 'The cattle also, concerning the rising storm.' Here it is read as a דרשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of cases about prayer: no prayer, prayer with no answer, and now prayer that was answered but led to pride.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One whose prayer is answered and who becomes proud brings Divine anger into the world (from 'מקנה אף על עולה').

steps.title: Two scholars who quarrel stir up anger
steps.stepSummary: רבא uses the same verse to teach that two תלמידי חכמים in one city who are not gentle with each other in הלכה stir up anger and make it rise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Two Torah scholars who live in one city and are not pleasant to each other in their הלכה discussions arouse anger and make it rise up. As the verse says: 'Anger is acquired by one who raises himself up.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second use of the same verse, 'מקנה אף על עולה'. This time it is about scholars who fight with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word מקנה is read as 'jealousy' (from קנאה). The scholars' rivalry 'stirs up' anger (מתקנאין באף) and 'raises it up' (מעלין אותו, from עולה). The new point is that bitter arguing between scholars, not only personal pride, brings anger into the world.

keyTerms.meaning: Are not pleasant or gentle with one another
They stir up anger (a wordplay on מקנה)
They make it rise up (a wordplay on עולה)

steps.whyThisMatters: Arguing about הלכה is part of Torah learning. The problem is not the argument itself. The problem is when scholars treat each other harshly.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין בְּעִיר אַחַת
phrases.english: Two Torah scholars who live in one city
and are not pleasant to one another in הלכה —
arouse anger and raise it up,
as it says: 'Anger is stirred up by one who rises up.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same verse used in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two scholars in one city who are harsh with each other in הלכה stir up Divine anger.

steps.title: The animals question the snake
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the verse about the snake: in the future, the animals will ask the snake what benefit it gets from biting, since it does not eat its victim. The snake will answer that the slanderer (בעל הלשון) gets no benefit either.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What is the meaning of the verse 'If the snake bites without a whisper, the master of the tongue has no advantage'? In the future, all the animals will gather and come to the snake and say to it: A lion mauls and eats, a wolf tears and eats, but you, what pleasure do you get? The snake will answer them: 'The master of the tongue has no advantage either.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains the same verse from קהלת whose ending was explained in step 11. He tells a parable about the snake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lion and the wolf at least eat what they kill, but the snake's bite gives it nothing. The snake turns the question around: 'בעל הלשון', the person who speaks לשון הרע, also gains nothing and still causes harm. So the person who speaks לשון הרע is worse than the snake.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the tongue; here, a person who speaks לשון הרע

steps.confusionAlert: In step 11, 'אין יתרון לבעל הלשון' meant someone who can pray but does not. Here ריש לקיש reads the same words in a different way, as being about a person who speaks לשון הרע.
steps.whatToRemember: Speaking לשון הרע causes harm and gives the speaker no real benefit. That makes it even worse than a snake's bite.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: What is the meaning of what is written:
'If the snake bites without a whisper,'
'then the master of the tongue has no advantage'?
In the future, they will gather and come —
all the animals — to the snake,
and they will say to it:
A lion mauls and eats,
a wolf tears apart and eats,
you, what pleasure do you have?
It says to them: 'The master of the tongue has no advantage either.'
phrases.notes: In other words: ask the slanderer first, since he also gains nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the verse from קהלת that רבי אמי first quoted in step 8 (and whose ending was explained in step 11), now applied to לשון הרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person who speaks לשון הרע harms others without gaining anything, so he is worse than the snake.

steps.title: Prayer is heard only with full sincerity
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches that a person's prayer is heard only if he places his soul in his hands. The source is 'נשא לבבנו אל כפים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: A person's prayer is heard only if he puts his soul in his palm. As the verse says: 'Let us lift up our heart with our hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of prayer. רבי אמי states a strict rule: prayer is heard only when it comes with complete sincerity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Putting one's soul in one's palm' means giving oneself over completely, so that the heart matches the words. The verse links the heart (לבבנו) with the hands (כפים) that are lifted in prayer. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts his soul in his palm; prays with total sincerity and devotion
Let us lift up our heart with our hands (איכה ג)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
A person's prayer is not heard

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מֵשִׂים נַפְשׁוֹ בְּכַפּוֹ,
phrases.english: unless he places his soul in his palm,
as it says: 'Let us lift up our heart with our hands.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֵין תְּפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם נִשְׁמַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new teaching about what makes a prayer accepted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prayer is accepted only when it comes with complete sincerity of heart.

steps.title: Challenge: even insincere prayer was forgiven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי from a verse that שמואל taught publicly. The people flattered God with their mouths while their hearts were not with Him, and still 'He, being merciful, forgives sin.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But שמואל appointed a speaker to repeat his lecture and taught: 'They flattered Him with their mouths and lied to Him with their tongues, their heart was not firm with Him, and they were not faithful to His covenant.' And even so, the next verse says: 'But He is merciful and forgives sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אמי's rule. A verse seems to show that God accepts even prayers that are not sincere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said that only a fully sincere prayer is heard. The verses in תהלים describe people whose words were fake and whose hearts were not with God. Yet God still forgave them. That seems to show that insincere prayer can also be accepted, which contradicts רבי אמי. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)
Here: a speaker who repeated the teacher's lecture aloud to the crowd

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word אמורא does not mean a sage of the גמרא period. It means the person who stood next to the teacher and announced his words loudly to the audience.

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אוֹקֵים שְׁמוּאֵל אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ וּדְרַשׁ:
phrases.english: But Shmuel set up a speaker for himself and taught:
'They flattered Him with their mouths'
'and with their tongues they lied to Him,'
'and their heart was not firm with Him,'
'and they were not faithful to His covenant,'
and even so —
'But He is merciful, He forgives sin, etc.'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא אוֹקֵים שְׁמוּאֵל אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי אמי's rule from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's claim that prayer is heard only with full sincerity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verses in תהלים describe insincere prayer (mouth without heart), yet God still forgave. This suggests that sincerity is not required for prayer to be accepted.

steps.title: Individual prayer versus community prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 18. רבי אמי was speaking about an individual. The verse שמואל taught is about a community (ציבור).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here (רבי אמי) is speaking about an individual. There (the verse) is speaking about a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it asked in step 18. It shows that the two sources are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual's prayer is heard only if his heart is truly in it, just as רבי אמי said. But when a whole community prays, God accepts the prayer even if the hearts are not fully sincere, in the merit of the group. So the verse about insincere people being forgiven describes a ציבור, and the contradiction is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This phrase opens an answer that settles a contradiction.
An individual, one person praying alone
A community or congregation praying together

steps.whatToRemember: An individual needs a sincere heart for his prayer to be heard. A ציבור is answered even when its prayer is lacking.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a major source for the special power of תפילה בציבור. It is a big reason to pray with a מנין.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: here, regarding an individual,
phrases.notes: "Here" refers to רבי אמי's rule that prayer requires placing one's soul in one's hands.

phrases.english: there, regarding a community.
phrases.notes: "There" refers to the verse שמואל taught, where insincere people were still forgiven.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּיָחִיד, כָּאן בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 18 against רבי אמי's teaching in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by context): the two sources speak about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי אמי's rule, that prayer needs a fully sincere heart, applies to every prayer, so the verse seemed to contradict it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי's rule applies to an individual. A ציבור is answered even without full sincerity.

steps.title: Rain falls only in the merit of faithful people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches that rain falls only because of בעלי אמנה, faithful and trustworthy people. He brings a verse from תהלים as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Rain falls only for the sake of faithful people, as it says: "Truth springs up from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching of רבי אמי. This one is about rain, which is the main topic of מסכת תענית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links two things: "truth" growing from the earth and "righteousness" coming down from heaven. When people below are truthful and faithful, God sends blessing from above, and rain is that blessing. So people's honesty and faith are what bring the rain down.

keyTerms.meaning: Faithful people: people who are trustworthy and who trust in God
"Truth springs up from the earth" (תהלים פ״ה:י״ב)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Rain does not fall
except for the sake of faithful people,
as it is stated: "Truth springs up from the earth
and righteousness looks down from heaven."
phrases.notes: Blessing, meaning rain, comes down in response.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֵין גְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל בַּעֲלֵי אֲמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same speaker, רבי אמי. It returns to the topic of rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain comes in the merit of faithful people, as learned from "אמת מארץ תצמח".

steps.title: The weasel and the pit show how great faith is
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches how great faithful people are, using the story of the חולדה (weasel) and the pit. He then builds a קל וחומר: if trusting in a weasel and a pit had such power, trusting in God has far more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אמי said: Come and see how great faithful people are. From where do we know this? From the weasel and the pit. If someone who trusted in a weasel and a pit was answered like this, then someone who trusts in the Holy One, Blessed be He, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives another teaching about faithful people. He points to a well-known story and then reasons from it with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, a young man and a young woman promised to stay faithful to each other. They named a weasel and a pit as their witnesses. When he broke the promise, those very "witnesses" carried out justice, and the woman's trust was proven right. If trust placed in a weasel and a pit was backed up like that, then trust placed in God is surely rewarded even more.

keyTerms.meaning: A weasel or marten. In the story, it was one of the witnesses to the promise.
A pit. In the story, it was the other witness.
All the more so. This phrase ends a קל וחומר.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא here only mentions the story briefly; it does not tell it. You need the background (given in the Sefaria translation and in רש״י) to understand the proof.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גְּדוֹלִים בַּעֲלֵי אֲמָנָה,
phrases.english: Come and see how great faithful people are,
From where do we know it? From the weasel and the pit.
phrases.notes: This refers to the story of the promise witnessed by a weasel and a pit.

phrases.english: Now if one who trusts in a weasel and a pit is treated like this,
one who trusts in the Holy One, Blessed be He,
all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גְּדוֹלִים בַּעֲלֵי אֲמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אמי's praise of בעלי אמנה from step 20, adding a story and a קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Faith is rewarded. If trust in a weasel and a pit was backed up, trust in God is surely rewarded.

steps.title: One who is exacting with himself is judged exactly from above
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that a person who is strict and exacting with himself on earth is judged in an exact way in Heaven. He uses the same verse רבי אמי used for rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whoever is exacting with himself below is judged exactly from above, as it says: "Truth springs up from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן. It reads the same verse in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the verse is not about rain. It describes a match between what happens below and what happens above. When a person holds himself to a strict standard of righteousness on earth, Heaven judges him by that same strict standard, so that he can keep growing.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is exacting with himself and holds himself to a strict standard of righteousness
From below, meaning here on earth

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same verse רבי אמי used in step 20, but רבי יוחנן reads it for a completely different idea. Do not mix up the two teachings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whoever is exacting with himself below,
they judge him exactly from above,
as it is stated: "Truth springs up from the earth
and righteousness looks down from heaven."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַמַּצְדִּיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that uses the same verse as step 20 for a different lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: How a person conducts himself below sets how he is judged above. Being exacting with oneself brings exact judgment from Heaven.

steps.title: A different verse for the same idea
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין, quoting רב הונא, learns רבי יוחנן's idea from a different verse: "And according to Your fear is Your wrath."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב הונא: We learn it from here: "And according to the fear of You is Your wrath."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source for the same teaching in step 22. רב הונא learns the idea from a different verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says God's anger matches the level of a person's fear of Him. A person who is very God-fearing and careful is judged more strictly. This is the same idea as רבי יוחנן's, only from another פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From here. This word introduces a different source verse.
"And according to the fear of You is Your wrath" (תהלים צ׳:י״א)

steps.whatToRemember: How strictly a person lives (his יראת שמים) affects how strictly Heaven judges him. רבי יוחנן and רב הונא agree on the idea and bring different verses for it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav Huna said,
from here: "And according to the fear of You is Your wrath."
phrases.notes: God's wrath matches the person's level of fear of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative verse for רבי יוחנן's teaching in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idea that strictness below brings strict judgment above is learned from "וכיראתך עברתך".

steps.title: ריש לקיש brings a third verse for the same idea
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns רבי יוחנן's idea, that careful people are judged carefully in Heaven, from a verse in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: We learn it from here: 'You met the one who rejoices and does righteousness, those who remember You in Your ways. Behold, You were angry, and we sinned. On them the world stands, and we will be saved.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his own verse as the source for the idea from step 22. It is a third source, next to the one from רב הונא in step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse talks about people who do righteousness happily and remember God in His ways. Right after that it says 'You were angry.' This links God's strict anger to the righteous people themselves, so the people who are most careful are judged most carefully.

keyTerms.meaning: A major אמורא of ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
From here, used to introduce a different verse as the source
One who rejoices and does righteousness

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: from here
phrases.notes: He offers a different source for the same idea

phrases.english: "You met the one who rejoices and does righteousness,
those who remember You in Your ways;
behold, You were angry, and we sinned;
phrases.notes: God's anger is connected to the righteous people just described

phrases.english: on them the world stands, and we will be saved."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another verse for the same idea that רב הונא learned from a different verse in step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idea that God judges the careful righteous strictly is learned from 'הן אתה קצפת', which follows the description of those who do righteousness.

steps.title: Joy in suffering brings salvation to the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that one who accepts his יסורין with joy brings ישועה to the world, learned from the end of the same verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who is happy with the sufferings that come upon him brings salvation to the world, as it says: 'On them the world stands, and we will be saved.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי takes the last words of the same verse and draws a new lesson from them. A person who accepts suffering with joy brings salvation to the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse began with 'the one who rejoices.' רבי יהושע בן לוי reads its ending, 'on them the world stands, and we will be saved,' as describing that joyful person. The word עולם, 'world,' tells us that the salvation reaches the whole world, not only the person himself.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא of ארץ ישראל
One who is joyful in his sufferings
The world (here read as 'the whole world')

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a well-known idea: how a person reacts to hard times can bring blessing to everyone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anyone who is joyful in sufferings
that come upon him
brings salvation to the world,
as it is said: "On them the world stands, and we will be saved."
phrases.notes: 'Them' refers back to the sufferings, or to the one who rejoices in them

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּיִסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same verse ריש לקיש just quoted, but teaches a new lesson from its last words
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who rejoices in the sufferings that come upon him brings salvation to the world.

steps.title: Closed heavens are like a woman in labor who cannot give birth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains 'ועצר את השמים': when the heavens hold back rain, they are like a woman in labor who cannot give birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What does the verse mean, 'And He will close up the heavens'? When the heavens are closed up and do not bring down dew and rain, it is like a woman who has labor pains and cannot give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of rain. ריש לקיש explains a verse with a picture: closed heavens are like a woman stuck in labor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heavens are 'ready' to give rain, just as the woman is ready to give birth. Something blocks it, so there is pain with no result. The point is that a drought is painful, even for the heavens.

keyTerms.meaning: And He will close up the heavens (דברים 11:17)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
What is meant by what is written: "And He will close up the heavens"?
When the heavens are closed up
from bringing down dew and rain,
it is like a woman who has labor pains
and does not give birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the theme of righteous people and goes back to the topic of rain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Withheld rain is compared to a woman in labor who cannot give birth.

steps.title: The same word, 'closing,' is used for rain and for a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects step 26 to a teaching of ריש לקיש in the name of בר קפרא: the word עצירה appears both for rain and for a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what ריש לקיש said in the name of בר קפרא: 'Closing' is said about rain, and 'closing' is said about a woman,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the comparison in step 26 comes from. It begins a teaching that links rain and a woman through a shared word, and that teaching continues into the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'ועצר' about the heavens. It uses the same word for a woman whose womb is closed (בראשית 20:18). Because the same word appears in both places, the two cases are compared. The sentence is not finished here, and the next passage completes the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as, used to link a teaching to an earlier statement
A תנא from the generation between the תנאים and the אמוראים

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence ends with a comma. בר קפרא's teaching is not complete yet, so don't look for its conclusion here. It continues on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: And this is what Reish Lakish said
in the name of Bar Kappara:
"Closing" is said regarding rain,
and "closing" is said regarding a woman,
phrases.notes: "כי עצר עצר ה׳ בעד כל רחם" (בראשית כ׳:י״ח); continues on the next עמוד

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the word-link that supports the comparison made in step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word עצירה is used both for rain and for a woman, which sets up a comparison between them (completed on the next amud).
